meeting-summary-template.0: A meeting summary is the short recap people actually read. Full notes are for the record; a summary is for action, and if someone missed the meeting, it should tell them what changed and what they need to do in under a minute.
meeting-summary-template.1: Inside: a copy-ready template for meeting summary emails and docs, 4 real examples, and a 10-minute method for writing one.
meeting-summary-template.2: Usually 5 to 10 lines long, a meeting summary is a brief recap that tells attendees and stakeholders what was decided, who will do what, and what is still open. Less formal than minutes. Shorter than full notes.
meeting-summary-template.4: Use this template for meeting summary emails, Slack posts or docs. One screen holds it.
meeting-summary-template.5: What is missing? The discussion. Anyone who wants detail can follow a link to the full notes.
meeting-summary-template.6: Below is an email template for a meeting summary. Its subject line tells people what they are getting before they open it.
meeting-summary-template.7: Why put the count of decisions and actions in the subject line? People see at a glance that there is something for them.
meeting-summary-template.8: Adapt any of these 4 short meeting summary examples.
meeting-summary-template.10: Write the summary right after the meeting, while details are fresh. Then follow these 5 steps:
meeting-summary-template.11: Microsoft Teams, for one, can generate an AI recap for licensed users ([Teams recap](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/teams/meetings/recap-in-microsoft-teams)), but the same 5 steps apply when you review it. Can't name a decision or an action? Say so. "No decisions today; we will decide on X next week." Still useful.

meeting-summary-template.14: Roughly 15 minutes per hour of recording. Listening to it all takes an hour or more.
meeting-summary-template.15: Share the summary where your team already works, which for most teams means 1 of 3 places:
meeting-summary-template.16: Pick 1 channel per meeting series. Stick with it, so people know where to look.
meeting-summary-template.18: Before sending, run one quick check: could someone who missed the meeting act on this in 60 seconds? No? Cut until they could. Our [action items guide](https://lynkk.ai/blog/action-items-examples-template) has examples of clear action items.
meeting-summary-template.20: See [AI meeting summarizer tools](https://lynkk.ai/blog/team-meeting-summary-ai) for a full comparison of AI tools, or turn to [Claap's meeting summary guide](https://www.claap.io/blog/meeting-summary) as another useful reference when you want more writing guidance.
meeting-summary-template.21: A meeting summary should include the purpose, key decisions, action items with owners and due dates, open questions and the next meeting date. Decisions and actions go first. Link to the full notes, so anyone who missed the meeting can act on it in under a minute.
meeting-summary-template.22: Keep a meeting summary to 5 to 10 lines. Anyone who needs detail can follow a link to full notes or a recording. Running longer means you are recapping the discussion instead of the outcome, so cut until someone could act on it within 60 seconds.
